title: Where's the best place on your body to get shot?
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck open with a thank-you about the show being named a best of 2008 podcast on iTunes, then move to gun deaths and US gun ownership statistics, including Kennesaw, Georgia's gun-ownership law. They then take up the question of the best place on the body to get shot, explaining wound ballistics: kinetic energy transfer, bone shattering and fragmenting, cavitation in soft tissue, and hollow-point and full metal jacket bullets. They rule out the head, torso, spine, and major arteries in arms and legs, and conclude the hand or foot is the least-bad target, citing expert Ed Sizemore's advice to lie down and run. The episode closes with listener mail from Coral Clark about booger-flavored jelly beans and Bertie Botts Every Flavor Beans made by Jelly Belly's manufacturer.
topics: Cook County General Hospital brain gunshot survival

segments.title: Opening banter and iTunes award
segments.summary: Hosts greet listeners and thank fans and producer Jerry for the show being named a best of 2008 podcast on iTunes.

segments.title: Gun deaths and US gun ownership
segments.summary: Discussion of a study linking lax handgun laws to higher handgun death rates, US gun counts (270 million, about 90 per 100 people), India's gun numbers, and Kennesaw, Georgia's law requiring gun ownership.

segments.title: Introducing the topic and wound ballistics
segments.summary: Hosts set up the question of the best place to get shot and explain that wound ballistics, how bullets transfer kinetic energy to the body, determines the damage.

segments.title: Bone shattering, cavitation, and bullet types
segments.summary: Bones absorb energy and shatter into fragments that damage organs. Soft tissue suffers cavitation, a cavity up to thirty times the bullet's width. Full metal jacket and hollow point bullets are described, and bullets can travel unpredictably, with the JFK magic bullet theory and a Marine firing-range accident mentioned.

segments.title: Ruling out head, torso, and spine
segments.summary: Chest, torso, spine and head are rejected as targets. Ed Sizemore is cited on heart versus brain injury, and Cook County General Hospital data says about one-third to two-thirds of brain gunshot patients survived in the period cited.

segments.title: Arms, legs, hands and feet
segments.summary: Arms and legs are ruled out because of major arteries (femoral and brachial), with fatal blood loss in minutes. Hip nerve bundle is ruled out as painful. Hands and feet are judged the best targets because bones are thin and bullets likely pass through, with advice to lie down and run.

segments.title: Listener mail on booger jelly beans
segments.summary: Listener Coral Clark writes that Bertie Botts Every Flavor Beans are made by the Jelly Belly manufacturer with unusual flavors, correcting an earlier episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give the email address for listener mail and sign off.
